def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # The colored marks lie on the lattice intersections; the unmarked lattice
    # intersections retain the separator color.
    marker_colors = {7, 8}
    lattice_rows = [r for r in range(h) if any(v in marker_colors for v in grid[r])]
    lattice_cols = [c for c in range(w) if any(grid[r][c] in marker_colors for r in range(h))]
    # The large uniform interiors define the output's background color.
    background = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out = []
    for ri in range(len(lattice_rows)-1):
        row = []
        for ci in range(len(lattice_cols)-1):
            corners = (grid[lattice_rows[ri]][lattice_cols[ci]],
                       grid[lattice_rows[ri]][lattice_cols[ci+1]],
                       grid[lattice_rows[ri+1]][lattice_cols[ci]],
                       grid[lattice_rows[ri+1]][lattice_cols[ci+1]])
            v = corners[0]
            row.append(v if v in marker_colors and all(x == v for x in corners) else background)
        out.append(row)
    return out

 "content": "from collections import Counter
from math import gcd

def _complete_axis(coords, limit):
    coords = sorted(set(coords))
    if len(coords) >= 2:
        step = 0
        for a, b in zip(coords, coords[1:]):
            step = gcd(step, b-a)
        # A frame edge can be unmarked when all of its corner symbols are
        # the neutral lattice color, so extend one regular cell backward.
        if step and coords[0] >= step:
            coords = [coords[0]-step] + coords
    return [x for x in coords if 0 <= x < limit]

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    marks = {7, 8}
    rows = _complete_axis([r for r in range(h) if any(x in marks for x in grid[r])], h)
    cols = _complete_axis([c for c in range(w) if any(grid[r][c] in marks for r in range(h))], w)
    # Background is the dominant color filling the cells between lattice lines.
    background = Counter(x for row in grid for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out = []
    for i in range(len(rows)-1):
        outrow = []
        for j in range(len(cols)-1):
            corners = (grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j+1]],
                       grid[rows[i+1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i+1]][cols[j+1]])
            color = corners[0]
            outrow.append(color if color in marks and all(x == color for x in corners) else background)
        out.append(outrow)
    return out
"
}
